note_tweet.text:
We believe the compute shortage is a software problem.

Over the past few weeks, we shared some of the results which corroborated this idea. At inference time, Language Models are usually over-parameterized and over-precise by orders of magnitude. Compression allows our customers to run frontier intelligence on the nodes they already own or rent.

Over the coming weeks, we're excited to share a series on new GPU primitives for recursive AI R&D, allowing customers to squeeze more discovery per GPU dollar and wield more control of constrained hardware.

note_tweet.text:
Law discovery is a scientific puzzle. The agent gets 40 read-outs from made-up instruments. Each log was generated by one hidden formula plus some noise, and the job is to discover the formula for every one.

Here we benchmark on:
•    Straight lines and power laws (6 datasets).
•    Standard shapes like saturating or exponential curves (9).
•    Two inputs combined inside one term (8).
•    Kinks, caps and thresholds (7).
•    Oscillation and damped ringing (4).
•    Ones that need a dimensional or symmetry argument (6).

Read more about how we quantize LLMs to generalize retention for unseen, long-horizon tasks like Law Discovery:
https://t.co/SQqfofGQEM

Mach 2 Additive Medium (1.7 bit Qwen 3.8 Flash-Next): https://t.co/aZF9IZHCA0

data.text:
Law discovery is a scientific puzzle. The agent gets 40 read-outs from made-up instruments. Each log was generated by one hidden formula plus some noise, and the job is to discover the formula for every one.

Here we benchmark on:
•    Straight lines and power laws (6 datasets).

note_tweet.text:
A key challenge with 2-bit or ternary LLMs is that they tend to collapse over long horizons and underperform full precision LLMs. So we hid 40 physical symmetries, ranging from phase transitions to permutation invariance to energy dissipation, in noisy instrument logs, and benchmarked the ability to discover these laws.

Quantized to just 1.7 bits per weight, Qwen 3.8 Flash-Next (125b) outperforms Qwen 3.8 27b while being even smaller in memory.

note_tweet.text:
Local models and your subscriptions, in any harness
Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode can all run on local models in Mach Studio, with no extra setup. Use your own subscriptions when you want a frontier model, switch to a local one when you hit a session limit or the task doesn't need the Fable or Astra, and keep the same session going either way. You pick the harness and the model separately, and you can change either one with a click.

As we prepare to roll out the fastest dedicated deployments for Kimi K3.1 and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, we wondered how far we could really push compression for inference.

So we quantized the MaleCNS fruit fly connectome to 0.45 bits per synapse: 124 million strengths in <7 MB, with neurons still firing like the original’s (r=0.97).
